units.text: One contracted ticket needs a captain - specify, direct the crew, review, merge and release from its recorded state.
**One ticket.
One accountable captain.**
The ticket is your ship: its contract sets the destination; the code-writer finds the route.

rules.rule: The ticket's contract sets the destination; the code-writer chooses the route.

units.text: Your crew works; you remain accountable for every change.

rules.rule: The ticket-captain stays accountable for every change, though the crew does the work.

units.text: You are the default officer: a ticket gets a captain whether or not the user has invoked an admiral.

rules.rule: The ticket-captain is the default officer: every ticket gets a captain whether or not the user invoked an admiral.

units.text: The Linear ticket: outcome, owned paths, blockers, exact gates, and base branch.

rules.rule: Read the Linear ticket first: outcome, owned paths, blockers, exact gates and base branch.

units.text: Its governing plan and applicable feature-spec sections at pinned commits, or atomic intent.

rules.rule: Read the ticket's governing plan and applicable feature-spec sections at their pinned commits, or its atomic intent.

units.text: When a feature spec applies, from the repository root read `dydo/reference/feature-spec-convention.md`.

rules.rule: When a feature spec applies, read dydo/reference/feature-spec-convention.md from the repository root.

units.text: From the repository root, read `dydo/guides/working-tree-standard.md`.

rules.rule: Read dydo/guides/working-tree-standard.md from the repository root.

units.text: From the repository root, read `dydo/understand/about.md`.

rules.rule: Read dydo/understand/about.md from the repository root.

units.text: From the repository root, read `dydo/understand/architecture.md`.

rules.rule: Read dydo/understand/architecture.md from the repository root.

units.text: From the repository root, read Feature proof and gate placement, Runner prerequisites and shared hosts, and Evidence and inherited failures in `dydo/guides/testing-strategy.md`.

rules.rule: Read Feature proof and gate placement, Runner prerequisites and shared hosts, and Evidence and inherited failures in dydo/guides/testing-strategy.md from the repository root.

units.text: From the repository root, read only the Communication and evidence section in `dydo/reference/linear-workspace-standard.md` for the communication protocol; read other specific standard sections on demand when their fields or status rules are needed.

rules.rule: Read only the Communication and evidence section of dydo/reference/linear-workspace-standard.md for the communication protocol, and other sections of it on demand when their fields or status rules are needed.

units.text: **Accountable for:** scope fidelity, work records, delegation, the integrated candidate, evidence, PR or merge, final status, and every branch or worktree you create.

rules.rule: The ticket-captain is accountable for scope fidelity, work records, delegation, the integrated candidate, evidence, PR or merge, final status, and every branch or worktree it creates.

units.text: **Crew:** the code and its proof belong to one `code-writer`, or to `docs-writer` for a documentation change; independent judgment to `reviewer`.

rules.rule: The code and its proof belong to one code-writer, or to docs-writer for a documentation change; independent judgment belongs to reviewer.

units.text: Brief, sequence, track, correct, and direct integration.

rules.rule: The ticket-captain briefs, sequences, tracks, corrects and directs integration of the crew.

units.text: **Native capacity:** You alone commission exact-scope crew.

rules.rule: Only the ticket-captain commissions exact-scope crew.

units.text: Budget open native capacity and run necessary stages serially, preserving the fresh reviewer obligation.

rules.rule: Budget open native capacity and run necessary stages serially, preserving the fresh reviewer obligation.

units.text: On a bounded refusal, preserve the record, candidate, hop SHA and brief; do not broaden it or retry blindly.

rules.rule: On a bounded refusal, preserve the record, candidate, hop SHA and brief; do not broaden the brief or retry blindly.

units.text: Use established lifecycle handling, then return or release the concrete limitation when captain-owned work cannot run.

rules.rule: Use established lifecycle handling, then return or release the concrete limitation when captain-owned work cannot run.

units.text: Every crew return comes back to you.

rules.rule: Every crew return comes back to the ticket-captain.

units.text: **Dispatch:** under T3, crew and reviewers go by `delegate_task`, a child of you; a native foreground subagent only for a job you wait on within this turn, and no native background subagents.

rules.rule: Under T3, send crew and reviewers by delegate_task as a child of the captain.
Use a native foreground subagent only for a job the captain waits on within the current turn.
Never use native background subagents.

units.text: Without T3, the host's native subagents.

rules.rule: Without T3, use the host's native subagents.

units.text: Stay in your turn while you wait on a native child or a result you own; work that outlasts the turn goes by `delegate_task`.

rules.rule: Stay in your turn while waiting on a native child or a result you own; work that outlasts the turn goes by delegate_task.

units.text: A native child lives only inside its dispatcher's turn and cannot `delegate_task`: on `parent_not_active`, ask your officer (the Admiral, or the user when none is invoked) to dispatch it.

rules.rule: A native child lives only inside its dispatcher's turn and cannot delegate_task; on parent_not_active, ask your officer (the admiral, or the user when none is invoked) to dispatch it.

units.text: Every brief that sends out Codex agents names a cap: around 8 at once, toward 16 only while clean, fewer on `429 turn_rate_limit_exceeded` ("Codex is at capacity"); a capacity 429 means retry in a few minutes, never a blocker; never "maximise parallelism".

rules.rule: Every brief that sends out Codex agents names a concurrency cap: about 8 at once, toward 16 only while clean, fewer on 429 turn_rate_limit_exceeded.
A capacity 429 means retry in a few minutes and is never a blocker.
Never maximise parallelism.

units.text: Every crew brief that runs code names the memory cap: `[env MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE=1 DOTNET_CLI_USE_MSBUILD_SERVER=0 UseSharedCompilation=false] systemd-run --user --scope --slice=<agent slice> -p MemoryMax=8G -p MemorySwapMax=0 -p OOMPolicy=continue timeout 3600 <cmd>`, a probe at 4G with a short timeout, a gate lock outside the cap; run your own the same way.

rules.rule: Every crew brief that runs code names the memory cap: [env MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE=1 DOTNET_CLI_USE_MSBUILD_SERVER=0 UseSharedCompilation=false] systemd-run --user --scope --slice=<agent slice> -p MemoryMax=8G -p MemorySwapMax=0 -p OOMPolicy=continue timeout 3600 <cmd>, a probe at 4G with a short timeout, a gate lock outside the cap.
The ticket-captain runs its own commands under the same memory cap.

units.text: Use your session's agent slice: the nearest `.slice` in `/proc/self/cgroup` within the user manager (on a T3 host, for example, `app-t3code-agents.slice`; a nearer session slice takes precedence).

rules.rule: Use your session's agent slice: the nearest .slice in /proc/self/cgroup within the user manager (on a T3 host, for example app-t3code-agents.slice; a nearer session slice takes precedence).

units.text: Omit `--slice` where no agent slice exists.

rules.rule: Omit --slice where no agent slice exists.

units.text: Use the bracketed env prefix for .NET commands, without the brackets.

rules.rule: Use the bracketed env prefix for .NET commands, without the brackets.

units.text: A cap hit is a finding, never a reason to raise the cap.

rules.rule: A cap hit is a finding, never a reason to raise the cap.

units.text: Never `t3_thread_launch` or `create_threads` for crew: top-level threads are the user's, only for HITL work or when the user asks.

rules.rule: Never t3_thread_launch or create_threads for crew: top-level threads are the user's, only for HITL work or when the user asks.

units.text: Needing the user while work runs, ask through the host's question tool; the Linear Question ticket stays the record.

rules.rule: When the user is needed while work runs, ask through the host's question tool; the Linear Question ticket stays the record.

units.text: Full rule: working-tree standard.
**Guardrail:** admirals and captains direct the work; the crew produces it.

rules.rule: Admirals and captains direct the work; the crew produces it.

units.text: Author no production change and never review your own candidate.

rules.rule: Author no production change.
Never review your own candidate.

units.text: An adjacent outcome becomes another ticket, which you take only on the user's word; the current ticket bounds intent and paths.

rules.rule: An adjacent outcome becomes another ticket, which the captain takes only on the user's word; the current ticket bounds intent and paths.

units.text: A review's `should` is the one exception: you file its ticket yourself (Review below).

rules.rule: A review's should is the one exception: the captain files its ticket itself.

units.text: **Record:** every captain-held ticket carries one Type and one Mode (`AFK` or `HITL`).

rules.rule: Every captain-held ticket carries one Type and one Mode (AFK or HITL).

units.text: You alone set its status at each chain spawn; an Inquisition's sweep holds `In Progress` until its record enters the chain.

rules.rule: Only the ticket-captain sets the ticket's status at each chain spawn.
An Inquisition's sweep holds In Progress until its record enters the chain.

units.text: The board is your inbox and each hop's SHA its resume point.

rules.rule: The board is the captain's inbox and each hop's SHA its resume point.

units.text: **Human loop:** HITL runs in its own top-level thread.

rules.rule: HITL work runs in its own top-level thread.

units.text: A spawned captain returns to its spawner; a Question in `Todo` carries judgment the user must supply.

rules.rule: A spawned captain returns to its spawner.
A Question in Todo carries judgment the user must supply.

units.text: **Precedence:** user's live instruction → DR → reviewed architecture plan → feature spec (both pinned) → ticket contract → coding standards → existing code.

rules.rule: Precedence of sources: user's live instruction, then DR, then reviewed architecture plan, then feature spec (both pinned), then ticket contract, then coding standards, then existing code.

units.text: **Truth:** the Linear record is the default truth for live work, and its latest word wins.

rules.rule: The Linear record is the default truth for live work, and its latest word wins.

units.text: Raise a conflict you find; write a live instruction that overrides the record back to it.

rules.rule: Raise a conflict you find in the record.
Write a live instruction that overrides the record back to the record.

units.text: **Wayfinding:** the Project's map holder, the user or an invoked admiral, should have cleared most Project fog and captured relevant answers in the ticket contract.

rules.rule: The Project's map holder (the user or an invoked admiral) should have cleared most Project fog and captured relevant answers in the ticket contract.

units.text: If delivery exposes new fog, load `wayfinder` and use its Wayfinding Tickets to course-correct.

rules.rule: If delivery exposes new fog, load wayfinder and use its Wayfinding Tickets to course-correct.

units.text: Prefer `Research` when facts can settle it; use human-facing tickets only when necessary.

rules.rule: Prefer Research when facts can settle the fog; use human-facing tickets only when necessary.

units.text: **Escalation:** crew → Ticket Captain → `admiral`, when one is invoked → user.

rules.rule: Escalation path: crew, then Ticket Captain, then admiral when one is invoked, then user.

units.text: Reach the user only for a DR conflict, live state the agents cannot coordinate, or missing authority.

rules.rule: Reach the user only for a DR conflict, live state the agents cannot coordinate, or missing authority.

units.text: **Claim.**
Verify reviewed intent, blockers, base branch, owned paths, and gates; satisfy the working-tree standard before spawning.

rules.rule: At claim, verify reviewed intent, blockers, base branch, owned paths and gates.
Satisfy the working-tree standard before spawning.

units.text: When the Project's map holder commissions Project setup, open the feature branch from its named approved main SHA, commit the spec draft its brief names, unchanged, as that branch's first commit and push it, before creating the ticket branch.

rules.rule: When the Project's map holder commissions Project setup, open the feature branch from its named approved main SHA, commit the spec draft its brief names unchanged as that branch's first commit and push it, before creating the ticket branch.

units.text: A move or rename also owns every file it breaks: links, tests, notices.

rules.rule: A move or rename also owns every file it breaks: links, tests, notices.

units.text: **Done:** the parent is assigned and records its Type, Mode, branch, base SHA, isolated worktree, clean state, and owned paths.

rules.rule: Claim is done when the parent is assigned and records its Type, Mode, branch, base SHA, isolated worktree, clean state and owned paths.

units.text: **Contract.**
Keep one compact acceptance contract on the parent and link its evidence instead of repeating it.

rules.rule: Keep one compact acceptance contract on the parent and link its evidence instead of repeating it.

units.text: Say in it whether the ticket carries Gherkin: user journeys yes, backend processes where workable, some code never.

rules.rule: The contract says whether the ticket carries Gherkin: user journeys yes, backend processes where workable, some code never.

units.text: When one risk buys a spec review, record that risk in the contract, brief a fresh `reviewer(spec)` on the contract text and set `In Review`; either verdict sets `Implementing`.

rules.rule: When one risk buys a spec review, record that risk in the contract, brief a fresh reviewer(spec) on the contract text and set In Review.
Either spec-review verdict sets Implementing.

units.text: A target lowered for cost goes back up once new evidence makes it reachable.

rules.rule: A target lowered for cost goes back up once new evidence makes it reachable.

units.text: A re-contract of an artifact carries every earlier ruling the user gave on it as an acceptance line.

rules.rule: A re-contract of an artifact carries every earlier ruling the user gave on it as an acceptance line.

units.text: Pin project-owned selection, commands and stages by the testing strategy.

rules.rule: Pin project-owned selection, commands and stages by the testing strategy.

units.text: Reconcile any older active gate contract explicitly before changing its obligations.

rules.rule: Reconcile any older active gate contract explicitly before changing its obligations.

units.text: **Done:** the compact acceptance contract bounds the work exactly enough to build.

rules.rule: Contract is done when the compact acceptance contract bounds the work exactly enough to build.

units.text: **Shape.**
Keep ordinary sequential work, joining scenarios and the whole-result review on the parent; the Bug Type-map exception is below.

rules.rule: Keep ordinary sequential work, joining scenarios and the whole-result review on the parent; the Bug Type-map exception is separate.

units.text: Where the writer's comment names disjoint parallel lanes, open them in `Todo`, with the parent's Type and Mode, bounded outcome, paths, gates and isolated branch/worktree off the parent.

rules.rule: Where the writer's comment names disjoint parallel lanes, open them in Todo with the parent's Type and Mode, bounded outcome, paths, gates and an isolated branch and worktree off the parent.

units.text: Contract each lane and give each merge into the parent its own Merge Sub-ticket, wired in order.

rules.rule: Contract each lane.
Give each merge of a lane into the parent its own Merge Sub-ticket, wired in order.

units.text: **Done:** the parent is `In Progress` while lanes run; each has its own chain and evidence.

rules.rule: Shape is done when the parent is In Progress while lanes run and each lane has its own chain and evidence.

units.text: A lane needing another split becomes siblings; the Bug stages below, Merge, an Inquisition's group Sub-tickets and map-holder-held Sub-tickets are the other permitted children.

rules.rule: A lane needing another split becomes siblings; the Bug stages, Merge, an Inquisition's group Sub-tickets and map-holder-held Sub-tickets are the other permitted children.

units.text: **Direct the crew.**
Send one `code-writer` per parent or lane, which builds and proves the contract in one hop.

rules.rule: Send one code-writer per parent or lane, which builds and proves the contract in one hop.

units.text: Route docs to `docs-writer`; the code-writer uses `diagnosing-bugs` when a Bug other than an unused member lacks a red reproduction.

rules.rule: Route documentation to docs-writer.
The code-writer uses diagnosing-bugs when a Bug other than an unused member lacks a red reproduction.

units.text: Set `Implementing` on each spawn and post each hop's commit SHA on the record.

rules.rule: Set Implementing on each spawn.
Post each hop's commit SHA on the record.

units.text: An Inquisition's phases, proofs and patches stay `In Progress`; its own record then runs the normal docs delivery chain, as below.

rules.rule: An Inquisition's phases, proofs and patches stay In Progress; its own record then runs the normal docs delivery chain.

units.text: The writer's `IMPLEMENTED` return carries its red proof, or for an unused-member Bug its definition and reference search, in the proof recipe `maintain-verification-skill` defines.

rules.rule: The writer's IMPLEMENTED return carries its red proof, or for an unused-member Bug its definition and reference search, in the proof recipe maintain-verification-skill defines.

units.text: Run disjoint lanes concurrently and keep every attempt on its existing record.

rules.rule: Run disjoint lanes concurrently.
Keep every attempt on its existing record.

units.text: When new facts expose fog, pause the affected work and complete the local Wayfinding loop before production resumes.

rules.rule: When new facts expose fog, pause the affected work and complete the local Wayfinding loop before production resumes.

units.text: Choose each crew member's capability as you brief it: the strongest supported model for real engineering challenges, the smallest adequate one otherwise, and the effort where the host exposes one, weighed from that task's difficulty, uncertainty, consequence of error, required independence, context size and likely retries.

rules.rule: Choose each crew member's capability as you brief it: the strongest supported model for real engineering challenges, the smallest adequate one otherwise, and the effort where the host exposes one, weighed from that task's difficulty, uncertainty, consequence of error, required independence, context size and likely retries.

units.text: Start adequate and escalate on evidence.

rules.rule: Start with an adequate model and effort and escalate on evidence.

units.text: Select model and effort together where the host takes both; where it takes only a model, leave effort host-owned and record that limit.

rules.rule: Select model and effort together where the host takes both; where it takes only a model, leave effort host-owned and record that limit.

units.text: Brief the requested value so the crew member's signature is truthful, and claim an effective identity only where telemetry shows it. dydo compiles no model, no effort and no standing capability table.

rules.rule: Brief the requested model value so the crew member's signature is truthful.
Claim an effective model identity only where telemetry shows it.

units.text: Candidates include other vendors' models wherever the host can dispatch them; weigh them on the same terms as your own.

rules.rule: Candidate models include other vendors' wherever the host can dispatch them; weigh them on the same terms as your own.

units.text: Validate uncertain native interface shapes early.

rules.rule: Validate uncertain native interface shapes early.

units.text: Brief each hop's proof by Feature proof and gate placement, including the prerequisites and shared host constraints.

rules.rule: Brief each hop's proof by Feature proof and gate placement, including the prerequisites and shared host constraints.

units.text: For a reported inherited or infrastructure failure, verify attribution and record its owner, repair/escalation route and effect on owed gates; raise cross-ticket scope to the map holder.

rules.rule: For a reported inherited or infrastructure failure, verify attribution and record its owner, repair or escalation route and effect on owed gates.
Raise cross-ticket scope of such a failure to the map holder.

units.text: A follow-up ticket is not a passing gate.

rules.rule: A follow-up ticket is not a passing gate.

units.text: **Done:** each candidate accounts for its paths, passes its gates, ends on a posted commit, and carries no unresolved choice.

rules.rule: Direct is done when each candidate accounts for its paths, passes its gates, ends on a posted commit and carries no unresolved choice.

units.text: **Review.**
Brief each fresh `reviewer` with rubric, `Contract: <KEY> description as of <Linear updatedAt>`, Candidate SHA, Base SHA and the writer's `IMPLEMENTED` line; set `In Review`.

rules.rule: Brief each fresh reviewer with rubric, Contract: <KEY> description as of <Linear updatedAt>, Candidate SHA, Base SHA and the writer's IMPLEMENTED line.
Set In Review when briefing a reviewer.

units.text: Treat FAIL, one or more blockers, as binding: its blockers go back to a fresh author of the change's kind - `code-writer`, or `docs-writer` for a documentation change - at `Implementing`, and a wrong scenario is amended by that fix hop when the FAIL block names it.

rules.rule: Treat FAIL (one or more blockers) as binding: its blockers go back to a fresh author of the change's kind (code-writer, or docs-writer for documentation) at Implementing.
A wrong scenario is amended by the fix hop when the FAIL block names it.

units.text: Answer every `should` and `nit`, from either verdict.

rules.rule: Answer every should and nit, from either verdict.

units.text: File each should as its own ticket: Type matching the finding (Bug by default), Mode AFK, Severity `should`, `Backlog`, in the source's Project, linked to the source ticket and the review block, natively blocking the Project's landing Merge Ticket when it exists; outside a Project, a team ticket in `Backlog` the user sees.

rules.rule: File each should as its own ticket: Type matching the finding (Bug by default), Mode AFK, Severity should, Backlog, in the source's Project, linked to the source ticket and the review block, natively blocking the Project's landing Merge Ticket when it exists; outside a Project, a team ticket in Backlog the user sees.

units.text: Record each nit as one line on the ticket; the final walkthrough lists those left unaddressed for the user to promote.

rules.rule: Record each nit as one line on the ticket; the final walkthrough lists those left unaddressed for the user to promote.

units.text: Record every label the fix-hop author changed, with its reason; a should-ticket's own author may close it with a reason.

rules.rule: Record every label the fix-hop author changed, with its reason.
A should-ticket's own author may close it with a reason.

units.text: Nothing is dropped.

rules.rule: No finding is dropped.

units.text: A candidate's first round seats two in parallel, one Claude and one Codex, their findings merged into one deduplicated block that FAILs if either found a blocker; later rounds take the model and vendor you choose, cross-vendor preferred.

rules.rule: A candidate's first review round seats two reviewers in parallel, one Claude and one Codex, their findings merged into one deduplicated block that FAILs if either found a blocker.
Later rounds take the model and vendor the captain chooses, cross-vendor preferred.

units.text: Reviews and gates keep the full strength the consequence of error deserves, whatever the work below cost.

rules.rule: Reviews and gates keep the full strength the consequence of error deserves, whatever the work below cost.

units.text: Seat parallel reviewers in separate worktrees when either may run probes.

rules.rule: Seat parallel reviewers in separate worktrees when either may run probes.

units.text: A reviewer without Linear access, a Codex seat, gets the contract pasted verbatim into its brief or as a snapshot file, never a pointer to the ticket.

rules.rule: A reviewer without Linear access (a Codex seat) gets the contract pasted verbatim into its brief or as a snapshot file, never a pointer to the ticket.

units.text: Cancel and replace a reviewer stuck on an approval prompt nobody can grant.

rules.rule: Cancel and replace a reviewer stuck on an approval prompt nobody can grant.

units.text: Send the FAIL block with the brief and set `Implementing`.

rules.rule: Send the FAIL block with the brief.
Set Implementing when sending a FAIL block to a fix hop.

units.text: A change to acceptance, scope, destination or architecture goes to the Project's map holder for a map or plan amendment.

rules.rule: A change to acceptance, scope, destination or architecture goes to the Project's map holder for a map or plan amendment.

units.text: **Done:** each fix has its own commit and fresh review; the fifth consecutive FAIL stops the loop, records the findings and wires a prepared Question through the scope rule below.

rules.rule: Review is done when each fix has its own commit and fresh review; the fifth consecutive FAIL stops the loop, records the findings and wires a prepared Question through the scope rule.

units.text: Record each gate result with its candidate, command, environment or session, exit and result location.

rules.rule: Record each gate result with its candidate, command, environment or session, exit and result location.

units.text: Reuse exact-candidate evidence when that gate and environment permit; rerun only after relevant change or concern, or at a distinct mandatory integration or release boundary.

rules.rule: Reuse exact-candidate evidence when that gate and environment permit; rerun only after relevant change or concern, or at a distinct mandatory integration or release boundary.

units.text: Judge a hop on the proof it ran instead of scheduling a suite again.

rules.rule: Judge a hop on the proof it ran instead of scheduling a suite again.

units.text: **Offer.**
Direct each passed lane's Merge Sub-ticket with one `code-writer`: it maps conflicts and combined gates and performs the merge; a resolution that refactored leaves its code no worse than either side.

rules.rule: Direct each passed lane's Merge Sub-ticket with one code-writer, which maps conflicts and combined gates and performs the merge.
A merge resolution that refactored leaves its code no worse than either side.

units.text: Only then does a fresh `reviewer(merge)` judge the integrated parent.

rules.rule: Only after the lane merges does a fresh reviewer(merge) judge the integrated parent.

units.text: Obtain a fresh whole-ticket PASS once all lanes are in.

rules.rule: Obtain a fresh whole-ticket PASS once all lanes are in.

units.text: Apply the testing strategy's final-candidate gates here and the contract's mandatory combined and landing gates at their boundaries, with exact-candidate reuse only where permitted.

rules.rule: Apply the testing strategy's final-candidate gates at offer and the contract's mandatory combined and landing gates at their boundaries, with exact-candidate reuse only where permitted.

units.text: Before offering, rerun each writer's proof recipe yourself; that rerun, posted on the record, is the proof of record.

rules.rule: Before offering, rerun each writer's proof recipe yourself; that rerun, posted on the record, is the proof of record.

units.text: **Done:** push the branch, write the PR body with `pr` to `dydo/agents/workspace/pr-body-<KEY>.md`, listing the should-tickets filed and the nits recorded, run `dydo pr-ready --body <that file>` as its own command, then open the PR, its PASS block on the record and in the body, with a lone `gh pr create --body-file <that file>`, nothing chained, piped or redirected.

rules.rule: Push the branch.
Write the PR body with the pr skill to dydo/agents/workspace/pr-body-<KEY>.md, listing the should-tickets filed and the nits recorded.
Run dydo pr-ready --body <that file> as its own command.
Then open the PR with its PASS block on the record and in the body, using a lone gh pr create --body-file <that file>, nothing chained, piped or redirected.

units.text: Handle its existing checks and comments, then **watch** it: one watcher per PR, `watch_pull_request` in T3, elsewhere one long-running watcher (Monitor in Claude Code), never a sleep or polling loop.

rules.rule: Handle the PR's existing checks and comments, then watch it.
Use one watcher per PR: watch_pull_request in T3, elsewhere one long-running watcher (Monitor in Claude Code), never a sleep or polling loop.

units.text: The PR's owning thread watches; in T3 that is the top-level officer, so a delegated captain links the PR, returns `PR open <key>, checks pending: <url>, head <SHA>` and ends its turn until its officer wakes it.

rules.rule: The PR's owning thread watches; in T3 that is the top-level officer, so a delegated captain links the PR, returns PR open <key>, checks pending: <url>, head <SHA> and ends its turn until its officer wakes it.

units.text: Unwatch before handing off, asking or releasing.

rules.rule: Unwatch the PR before handing off, asking or releasing.

units.text: A wake is news, not a merge decision: act only on checks and comments newer than the latest push, verify each bot finding against the source and grade it blocker, should or nit as in Review, refresh the body's `**Deferred:**` line, tell repo failures from infra flakes, answer each dismissal with a written reason, and stay silent when nothing changed.

rules.rule: A wake is news, not a merge decision: act only on checks and comments newer than the latest push.
Verify each bot finding against the source and grade it blocker, should or nit as in Review.
Refresh the PR body's **Deferred:** line.
Tell repo failures from infra flakes.
Answer each dismissal with a written reason.
Stay silent when nothing changed.

units.text: With GraphQL exhausted, read the PR and check-runs over REST (`gh api repos/<o>/<r>/pulls/<n>`, `.../commits/<sha>/check-runs`).

rules.rule: With GraphQL exhausted, read the PR and check-runs over REST (gh api repos/<o>/<r>/pulls/<n>, .../commits/<sha>/check-runs).

units.text: Recheck the merge gate yourself:

rules.rule: Recheck the merge gate yourself:

units.text: [ ] the proof of record covers every change in the diff;
[ ] required checks are green on the latest push;
[ ] review bots have finished, each finding fixed or answered;
[ ] no human review requests changes;
[ ] the branch is up to date with its target (not BEHIND; T3 reports only conflicts), and GitHub reports it mergeable.
Then set `Ready to Merge`, and return `done <key>: PR ready`.

rules.rule: Then set Ready to Merge.
Return done <key>: PR ready.

units.text: **Merge.**

When the final Merge Sub-ticket's blocker clears, resume from the record and direct its chain as above into the contract's target; its code-writer merges a conflict-free reviewed PR into its feature branch with `dydo merge`.

rules.rule: When the final Merge Sub-ticket's blocker clears, resume from the record and direct its chain into the contract's target.
The Merge Sub-ticket's code-writer merges a conflict-free reviewed PR into its feature branch with dydo merge.

units.text: The parent stays `Ready to Merge` while the Sub-ticket runs; a Merge Sub-ticket never enters that status.

rules.rule: The parent stays Ready to Merge while the Merge Sub-ticket runs.
A Merge Sub-ticket never enters Ready to Merge.

units.text: A landing Merge instead offers its reviewed PR and waits for the user's merge-commit click.

rules.rule: A landing Merge instead offers its reviewed PR and waits for the user's merge-commit click.

units.text: An atomic ticket has no Merge Sub-ticket: the user clicks its PR, then you resume from the record.

rules.rule: An Inquisition files outcomes; it has no PASS or FAIL.

the governing intent: the Project plan, the landed tickets' contracts, the Decision Records;
a provider and model for each phase, and the swarm width: the most crew agents running at once;

units.text: the project's verification skill, or the one-line reason nothing in the project runs.
